senses.sense_definition: The political philosophy of Niccolò Machiavelli, emphasizing state power, cunning, and pragmatic realism above moral or ethical principles.

examples.text: The historian argued that the leader's foreign policy was an exercise in pure <w>Machiavellianism</w>.
Many scholars view <w>Machiavellianism</w> as a form of political realism rather than mere cynicism.

senses.sense_definition: A personality trait characterized by interpersonal manipulation, cold detachment, cynicism, and an indifference to conventional morality.

examples.text: Psychologists often study <w>Machiavellianism</w> as part of the Dark Triad of personality traits.
Individuals who score high in <w>Machiavellianism</w> are frequently skilled at manipulating colleagues for personal gain.

senses.sense_definition: An unscrupulous political maneuver or piece of deceitful statecraft.

examples.text: The leaked memo exposed the subtle <w>Machiavellianisms</w> taking place behind closed doors.
Citizens grew exhausted by the endless display of bureaucratic <w>Machiavellianism</w> in the capital.
